newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP to sell Dai Hung stake - papers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP to sell Dai Hung stake - papers.

text.p: Australian resources group The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd (BHP) has agreed to sell its 43.75 percent stake in Vietnam's Dai Hung offshore oil project to Malaysia's state-owned Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), Australian newspapers reported on Tuesday.

"The deal, completed in principle between the two companies, is awaiting ratification by the Vietnamese Government before being approved by the BHP board in Melbourne," The Australian Financial Review said.
A BHP spokesman said he could not comment on the reports.
"We're not making any comments at the moment," a BHP spokesman told Reuters.
BHP Managing Director John Prescott said in late December that BHP was in talks with Petronas over the stake.
Petronas already has a 20 percent stake in Dai Hung. The Vietnamese government's PetoVietnam has 15 percent and Total Sa and Sumitomo Corp have 10.625 percent each.

BHP, which fully wrote down its A$151 million Dai Hung investment in its 1995/96 accounts, had before its talks with Petronas been trying to renegotiate terms of its contract with PetroVietnam after estimates of the field's reserves were cut.
According to initial estimates, Dai Hung had recoverable oil reserves of 700 million barrels but this was later revised down to 100 million barrels.
